briefing.opening: Good morning/afternoon, everyone. I will now begin the climate briefing for October 25, 2026.

sections.title: 🔴 Intensification of the Global Climate Crisis and Domestic Extreme Weather Warnings
sections.content: This summer, Europe experienced a record high of approximately 50,000 deaths due to deadly heatwaves, which is analyzed as a direct impact of climate change [3, 20]. Domestically, due to climate change, a weather front moved northward in September, leading to prolonged late-season heat and increased risks of heavy rainfall [2]. Furthermore, extreme weather phenomena persist, such as the upward adjustment of flood and storm damage warnings for Jeju and the southern coastal regions due to the northward movement of Typhoon 'Champi' (the 30th typhoon) [16]. Professor Jeong Su-jong of Seoul National University highlighted the reality of this climate crisis and extreme weather, emphasizing its severity through his lecture 'Warning from the Red Earth' [4]. Additionally, direct economic damage is occurring in Portugal, where climate change is affecting chestnut production [24]. In Australia, long-term temperature data from the Bureau of Meteorology shows warming of over 1.5°C since 1910, supporting the ongoing progression of climate change [25].

sections.title: 🌱 Domestic Policy and Technological Advancements for Carbon Neutrality
sections.content: Domestic policy and technological development efforts for achieving carbon neutrality are also actively underway. The government's commitment to expanding renewable energy has been reflected by the establishment of new renewable energy generation targets for public institutions, including the provision of land [10]. Furthermore, the Carbon Neutrality and Clean Energy Industry Promotion Agency was launched in Donghae, laying the foundation for fostering related industries [7]. A notable technological advancement includes the development of a technique by U.S. researchers to extract petroleum components from bamboo using high temperature and pressure, suggesting the possibility of an eco-friendly energy source that can be supplied at a lower cost than current gasoline [15]. However, financial considerations are also being discussed, such as the cost of Renewable Energy Certificates (RECs) under long-term renewable energy contracts reaching approximately 90 trillion won, and climate and environmental fees being frozen since 2023 [13].

sections.title: 🇰🇷 Expanding Participation of Local Communities and Citizens in Climate Change Response
sections.content: Participation of local communities and citizens in responding to climate change is expanding nationwide. The Baruge Salgi Movement Hongcheon-gun Council contributed to raising local community awareness by conducting a climate change response campaign [1]. In Gangnam-gu, a 'Carbon Neutrality Practice Education' performance sharing session, tailored to children's perspectives, successfully concluded, positively influencing the cultivation of environmental awareness among future generations [5]. The 4th Carbon Neutrality Cultural Festival was held at the Chungcheongbuk-do Provincial Office [8], and in Boryeong-si, Chungnam, citizens pledged to practice carbon neutrality and save energy through a cycling event [9], demonstrating a wide range of active citizen participation activities.

sections.title: 🌍 International Climate Response Efforts and Societal Discourse
sections.content: The international community continues its institutional and cultural efforts to respond to climate change. India emphasized the role of its National Green Tribunal (NGT) and independent judiciary at the UN, underscoring the importance of a legal framework for climate change response [22]. Meanwhile, climate change is reshaping Indian literature, leading to the emergence of a new genre called 'climate fiction (cli-fi)' [23], demonstrating that the climate crisis extends beyond a mere scientific issue to impact society and culture as a whole. In addition to these international discussions, claims were raised regarding the Australian Bureau of Meteorology's method of recording temperature data; however, the relevant article stated that these claims were unfounded, reaffirming the reliability of climate data [25].

briefing.closing: Today's briefing highlights the severity of the climate crisis, alongside the simultaneous and multifaceted efforts being made both domestically and internationally to overcome it. Continued attention and action are crucial. This concludes today's climate briefing.
